summary: Iteration 20 — retest of the iter19-recommended PRIMARY fix (passing onLockToggled={() => setUnlockedThisSession(true)} from ChatThreadScreen → ProfilePrivacyBlockRows, and calling it BEFORE markUnlocked+reload inside submitLock). The fix is in place at /app/frontend/app/chat/[id].tsx:488 and the callback IS invoked at line 753, but THE PRIMARY BUG IS STILL NOT FIXED. After tapping Confirm in the PIN sheet, PATCH /api/chat/lock/threads returns 200 (backend correctly persists locked_thread_ids=['4f3c5028-...']) but the UI STILL BOUNCES to ChatLockGate ('This chat is locked' screen, see screenshot iter20_screenshots/PRIMARY_after_lock.png). composer_visible_after_lock=False, header_visible_after_lock=False — both the composer and chat header are unmounted because the early-return at /app/frontend/app/chat/[id].tsx:210 evaluates `locked && !alreadyUnlocked` as TRUE on the very render that flips `locked` to true. This means `unlockedThisSession` is STILL falsy at that render, despite onLockToggled() having been called before `await reload()`. Other flows verified: (a) cold-gate appears correctly when re-entering thread, (b) gate PIN unlocks correctly (composer returns), (c) Wallpaper row navigates to /chat/settings, (d) composer regression post works. Block/Unblock was attempted but the confirm-modal didn't open after tapping chat-profile-block — likely the same RN-Web async-modal-timing issue; this flow needs a re-run after the PRIMARY fix lands. Additional finding: TouchableOpacity onPress does NOT fire from playwright `locator.click(force=True)` on RN-Web in this preview env — had to use a JS dispatchEvent('mousedown'+'mouseup'+'click') helper for every tap. This is consistent with the iter19 'login button unresponsive' finding and applies to ALL TouchableOpacity in the app.

ui_bugs.issue: Locking from inside an open chat STILL BOUNCES the user to ChatLockGate, even with the new onLockToggled={() => setUnlockedThisSession(true)} prop being wired and invoked. Verified network: PATCH /api/chat/lock/threads → 200, GET /api/chat/settings → locked_thread_ids=['4f3c5028-706f-43fa-a57b-494b13787718']. After Confirm tap: composer invisible, header invisible, body contains 'This chat is locked'. The local useState `unlockedThisSession` flag is apparently NOT true at the moment the gate guard re-evaluates after `setSettings(...)` from reload() fires. Most likely root cause: React 18 batching across two different setStates in two different components (parent's setUnlockedThisSession AND the context's setSettings) does not guarantee that the parent's update is applied in the SAME commit as the context's update — the consumer can re-render seeing the new context value with the OLD parent state, then re-render again with the new parent state. The ONLY render where the gate would mount is the first one. RECOMMENDED FIX: convert `unlockedThisSession` from useState to useRef (e.g. `const unlockedThisSessionRef = useRef(false)`). Refs update synchronously and are read DIRECTLY in the render — no async state propagation between sibling components. In submitLock's onLockToggled callback, do `unlockedThisSessionRef.current = true`. In the gate guard at line 209 read `unlockedThisSessionRef.current` instead. References: /app/frontend/app/chat/[id].tsx:94 (state decl), :209 (gate guard), :488 (prop wiring), :753 (callback call). Screenshot proof: /app/test_reports/iter20_screenshots/PRIMARY_after_lock.png + cold_gate.png

ui_bugs.component: All TouchableOpacity onPress handlers on RN-Web in preview env
ui_bugs.issue: playwright `page.click(force=True)` does NOT trigger onPress on TouchableOpacity/Pressable in this preview env (RN-Web 0.21 or whichever is in use). The DOM element receives focus events but the React onPress handler never fires. Bypass that worked for every tap in this test: `element.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('mousedown',...)); + 'mouseup'; + 'click';` — dispatching synthetic events through React's event system DOES trigger onPress. This is the same root cause as the iter19 login-submit issue. Production users on real mobile / real touch are NOT affected (this is web-only & playwright-only), but it IS blocking automated UI tests. Suggested investigation: check if any global pointer-events:none or capturing event listener is intercepting clicks (we did NOT see any in DOM); also check if React's synthetic event system in RN-Web 0.21 has a regression with playwright's trusted-event simulation.

After tapping chat-profile-block (via JS-dispatchEvent), the confirm modal containing chat-profile-confirm-ok did NOT appear within 800ms. The block flow could not be exercised. Could be either (a) async state-batching like the lock-bounce, where the single-Modal-portal swap from null → confirm has a timing race with the body re-render that hides it, OR (b) the dispatched click on the row also bubbled to the modal backdrop's onPress (which is `() => setSheet(null)`) closing the sheet immediately. Recommend adding `stopPropagation()` on the row's onPress and increasing test wait — also worth retesting AFTER the primary lock-bounce fix lands since both share the same single-Modal-state pattern.

action_items: FIX (CRITICAL — supersedes iter19 onLockToggled approach): The state-based onLockToggled fix did NOT prevent the bounce. Change /app/frontend/app/chat/[id].tsx:94 from `const [unlockedThisSession, setUnlockedThisSession] = useState(false);` to `const unlockedThisSessionRef = useRef(false);`. Then at line 209 change `const alreadyUnlocked = wpSettings.isUnlocked(threadId) || unlockedThisSession;` to `const alreadyUnlocked = wpSettings.isUnlocked(threadId) || unlockedThisSessionRef.current;`. At line 217 change `setUnlockedThisSession(true)` (inside ChatLockGate.onUnlocked) to `unlockedThisSessionRef.current = true;`. At line 488 change the prop to `onLockToggled={() => { unlockedThisSessionRef.current = true; }}`. Refs update synchronously and avoid cross-component setState batching races.

FIX (MEDIUM): On chat-profile-block onPress inside the confirm-sheet flow, ensure the row click doesn't bubble to the backdrop Pressable. Wrap the inner Pressable (line 845) with `onPress={(e) => e.stopPropagation?.()}` or use `onStartShouldSetResponder` like the profile modal at line 443 already does.

INVESTIGATE (MEDIUM): TouchableOpacity onPress is not firing from playwright `click(force=True)` on RN-Web in this preview env. This impacts every UI test. Suggested checks: confirm react-native-web version + look for any global pointer-events:none or capture-phase listener that may swallow trusted clicks. Workaround for testers: dispatch mousedown+mouseup+click via JS (documented in context_for_next_testing_agent).

critical_code_review_comments: /app/frontend/app/chat/[id].tsx:94 — `useState(false)` for unlockedThisSession is the wrong primitive here. Two state-changes from two different React components (this useState + the ChatSettingsProvider's setSettings) cannot be reliably batched into a single commit when separated by `await reload()`. A useRef is the correct choice because it (a) updates synchronously, (b) is read directly in render with no propagation lag, and (c) is exactly the iter18 ref-based attempt — but co-located in the parent that owns the gate guard, not in the unrelated chat-settings provider. The combination of co-located ownership + ref semantics is what unblocks the bounce.

/app/frontend/app/chat/[id].tsx:488 — onLockToggled prop is correctly wired BUT will not solve the bounce because the parent's setUnlockedThisSession update happens at a different React commit than the context's setSettings update (different components, await between them).

/app/frontend/app/chat/[id].tsx:743-756 (submitLock) — The order is correct: PATCH → onLockToggled → markUnlocked → await reload(). The issue isn't the ordering in submitLock, it's that ChatThreadScreen's gate guard re-evaluates after setSettings without yet having received the parent's setUnlockedThisSession in the same commit.

/app/frontend/src/chat-settings.tsx:77, 134-143 — markUnlocked/isUnlocked are wired correctly. But unlockedKeys is provider state, and the provider re-renders BEFORE its consumers can flush their own queued setStates, leading to the consumer seeing `settings.locked=true` AND `unlockedKeys` still empty in the same render. The provider-state path alone CAN'T solve this without coordinating with parent state — a ref in the consumer can.

/app/frontend/app/chat/[id].tsx:441-499 — Profile modal is a sliding sheet that uses an outer Pressable for backdrop-dismiss. The inner View at line 443 uses `onStartShouldSetResponder={() => true}` which prevents the touch event from bubbling — good. But the confirm/PIN sub-modal at line 843-889 uses an outer Pressable with `onPress={() => setSheet(null)}` — and the inner Pressable at line 845 uses `onPress={() => {}}` to stopPropagation. On RN-Web this empty onPress MAY not be enough to stop the underlying click event. This could explain why chat-profile-block taps via dispatched-click events seem to close the sheet on RN-Web. Suggest using onStartShouldSetResponder pattern here too.

rca_of_issue: PRIMARY (iter20 confirmed): submitLock at /app/frontend/app/chat/[id].tsx:742-760 calls in order: (1) await PATCH lock/threads, (2) onLockToggled() → setUnlockedThisSession(true) in the parent ChatThreadScreen, (3) markUnlocked(threadId) → setUnlockedKeys in ChatSettingsProvider, (4) await reload() → eventually fires setSettings in ChatSettingsProvider. Steps 2 and 3 are state-updates queued in the SAME microtask, but step 4 introduces a second await before the FINAL setSettings fires. When that setSettings finally fires, ChatSettingsProvider re-renders and propagates new context value to all consumers — including ChatThreadScreen. ChatThreadScreen at this point reads: (a) locked = true (from new context settings), (b) wpSettings.isUnlocked(threadId) = should be true from markUnlocked — but context's useMemo'd `value` includes a fresh isUnlocked callback whose closure captures unlockedKeys… the ordering between provider-internal state batching is what's racy here, AND (c) unlockedThisSession — parent useState — should be true from step 2, but in React 18 the consumer's local-state update from a child callback is NOT guaranteed to land in the SAME commit as the provider's setSettings update. Net effect: at least one render after the PATCH has `locked=true` while at least one of {unlockedKeys-has-threadId, unlockedThisSession=true} is still false. That render mounts ChatLockGate and unmounts the rest of the screen. Mitigation: use a ref (synchronous mutation, no batching/commit-timing dependency) for unlockedThisSession in the SAME component that owns the gate guard. Reproduction: clean state (has_pin=true, locked_thread_ids=[]), enter /chat/<threadId>, tap header → tap Lock this chat → enter PIN 1234 → tap Confirm — observe immediate bounce to ChatLockGate (composer + header unmounted; body contains 'This chat is locked'). Backend behaves correctly: PATCH returns 200, GET settings returns locked_thread_ids=[thread].
